matches.rationale: Finding 7 identifies the implausible zero-barrier row for learned matching in Table 2. This directly detects the corrupted table data that is the core of GT1's data fabrication issue, even though the finding does not explicitly note the contradiction with the text.
Finding 2 explicitly flags the use of inf instead of sup in Equation 2 and explains why it contradicts the definition of LMC, matching GT2's method logic error exactly.

No finding mentions the unqualified overgeneralization about RoPE-based Transformers or the missing architectural caveat described in GT3. The abstract discrepancies identified are about different claims.
No finding points out the missing learning rate value η in Algorithm 1, which is the specific methodological omission in GT4.
No finding reports the fabricated citation 'Zhou et al., 2024' in the Related Work described in GT5.

Finding 6 catches the exaggerated promotional claim in the Introduction ('definitively proving that all neural networks exist in a single connected basin'), which matches GT6's description of absolute promotional language in that section.
Finding 1 directly identifies the arg min vs arg max error in Equation 3 and explains why maximization is required, fully matching GT7's logical contradiction in the weight matching objective.
No finding mentions the removal of the BookCorpus barrier discussion from Section 5; the existing findings do not address this specific omission of negative results.
Finding 8 highlights the undefined ⋄ operator used in Figure 2's explanation, exactly the missing definition described in GT9.
No finding discusses the misrepresentation of Figure 5 as showing 'perfect alignment' or the contradiction with the eigenangle analysis specified in GT10.
No finding identifies the undisclosed asymmetric application of temperature scaling for Tiny ImageNet, which is the experimental protocol issue in GT11.
GT12 concerns the complete removal of the Limitations section (Appendix A). Finding 9 instead observes that a limitations section is present but contains internal contradictions, a different issue.
No finding reports the exaggerated claim that learned matching produces 'the broadest region of near-zero deviation' in Figure 4 or the misrepresentation of the contour baseline, as in GT13.
No finding addresses the misattribution of Git Re-Basin to Singh and Jaggi [2020] in the Related Work, which is the citation manipulation issue in GT14.

Both Finding 3 and Finding 4 capture the claim in the Conclusion that 'permutation symmetries alone are sufficient,' which is the contradictory statement noted in GT15 (whether contrasted with the Abstract or Introduction, the underlying corrupted claim is identical).
